## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the refresh before merge because adding files can erase the stored fingerprints that verification needs to detect edits.

## Changes

The pull request adds two helpers that update the JSON fingerprint manifest. `refresh_fingerprints` writes a digest for every supplied name, while `register_new_files` writes digests only for unlisted names.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve tracked digests when adding files — Refreshing `["tracked.txt", "new.txt"]` after `tracked.txt` was edited replaces its stored digest, so `verify()` reports success. The refresh loop assigns a new digest for every supplied name. — Adding a file can cause verification to accept edits to a tracked file that the refresh also includes. — Fix: Reuse the existing-entry check from `register_new_files`.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:25 — correctness — Keep the manifest out of its own fingerprint list — Passing `["fingerprints.json"]` when the manifest is an unlisted file under the content root makes verification fail after either helper succeeds. Both helpers record the digest of the manifest before rewriting it. — A file scan that includes the manifest can cause verification to fail even when all other files are intact.
- app/integrity.py:18 — correctness — Convert relative Path inputs to manifest keys — Passing `[Path("new.txt")]` for an existing file makes either helper raise `TypeError` during JSON serialization. The file lookup accepts the `Path`, but the helper also uses it as a JSON object key. — Callers that pass root-relative `Path` objects cannot add those files to the manifest. — Fix: Convert each name to a string before lookup and insertion.

## Suggestions

- tests/test_integrity.py:18 — tests — Assert that an empty refresh preserves entries — With `names=[]`, the assertion passes even if refresh replaces the populated manifest with `{}`. `verify()` returns true when there are no entries to check. — The test would miss a regression that clears every stored fingerprint during an empty refresh. — Fix: Assert that the manifest entries are unchanged after the empty refresh.
